items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: They say he was Shelton Brooks, you know. So I didn't know his name at that time, and I asked him, I say, "Mister, I says -- what should I do?"

ctx.x: Now, I didn't have those bottle tops on my feet this time, you see, on the stage, but I was barefooted, see. The people wanted to laugh, you see, and I didn't think really that I could dance, you know. I was just learning these steps, you see. So a fellow was standing in the wings offstage, and as I went off the stage and people was applauding and saying, more, more, dance, dance, you know, because they loved dancing in the South, you see, it was very popular. That was on account of Jack Wiggins, John Bowles, you…

And this fellow was standing offstage, and I knew who he was. They say he was Shelton Brooks, you know. So I didn't know his name at that time, and I asked him, I say, "Mister, I says -- what should I do?" And I had a big smile on my face, you see, and he said, "Well, you keep that smile on your face and just walk just off the curtain there and bend

over halfway to the people that's setting out there applauding for you. And you do the same thing, you turn to the -- see the gentleman with the stick in his hand that's down there leading the orchestra? I say, 'Yes, sir.'
